accuracy.evidence: Every sum in learn/counton_art.js was recomputed: jars 5+2=7, 4+3=7, 6+1=7; track 4+3=7, 6+2=8, 3+4=7; bigger-first 2+6, 1+5, 3+7 with the correct count lengths (2, 1, 3 counts from the larger number); bus 7+2=9, 5+3=8, 8+1=9; fingers 8+2, 5+3, 6+4. Parameterised items use {=n+k} and validate at range corners. The strategy order (count all, count on from first, count on from larger) matches Carpenter and Moser (1984) and Fuson (1982); the EYFS link is Development Matters 2021 'one more than', and the Year 1 link is the National Curriculum statement on adding one-digit numbers. No claim that counting on suits large addends: the adult text limits it to adding about 1 to 4.

misconceptions.evidence: Targets the documented counting-on slips: saying the first number again for the first new object (jar refuses a car before the jar is tapped; bus keypad answer n+k-1 gets 'one short: you said 7 for the first person'; p4, m8, challenge tag 'from'); counting the start square as a jump (track 'Stay on 4' is refused, predict 6 vs 7, m4, tag 'jump'); counting only the new ones (bus answer k, tag 'all'); starting from the smaller number (scene 3 refuses with the long count shown, p3, m6, tag 'small'); believing order changes the total (predict 2+6 vs 6+2, p5, tag 'turn'); and losing track of how many were added (finger scene refuses too many, tag 'fingers').

lab_distinct.evidence: flagcounton is built round the counting-on mechanism itself: a jar that hides the first group so only its numeral can be said, a frog whose jumps (not squares) are counted with arcs numbered 1, 2, 3, a choice of start number that shows the length of the count, and fingers that stop the count. It is not flagcountup (counting up to subtract), flagdoubles (two equal groups) or flagguess (estimate then count); the gate shows it under 30% shingle overlap with every other lab.

lab_teaches.evidence: The learner discovers the idea before the text says it: the jar cannot be opened, so the only way on is to say its number and count on; the track only accepts the next square, so the start square visibly is not a jump; picking the smaller number gives the right total but prints a long count, so the learner finds the quicker start; each completion message then names the rule (for example 'On 4, 3 jumps lands on 7, not 6. The square you start on is not a jump').

predictions.evidence: Two predictions each with a tempting wrong option that the lab then disproves: 'The frog is on 4. It jumps 3 times. Where does it land?' (6, from counting the start square, vs 7; the track refuses Stay on 4 and lands on 7), and 'Is 2 and 6 the same as 6 and 2?' (No, 2 and 6 is less, vs Yes, both make 8; scene 3 shows both starts give 8).

challenge_feedback.evidence: Six challenge questions rotate answer order; each wrong option carries a tag with its own message: 'from' (you said the first number again; the first new one is one more), 'all' (only the ones you add), 'jump' (the start square is not a jump), 'small' (you can, but start from the bigger number), 'turn' (order does not change the total, 3 and 6 is 9 and 6 and 3 is 9), 'fingers' (fingers count only the ones you add).

readability.evidence: Kid text uses short sentences and number words a 4 to 5 year old hears (jar, cars, count on, bigger); the validator keeps kid text within grade 6.5 and adult within 9.5. Lab prompts are one or two short sentences, numerals are drawn large (jar numeral about a third of the jar height), and spoken feedback reads the count aloud ('5 … 6, 7').

no_filler.evidence: Every kid paragraph carries one step of the method (hidden group, count on, do not repeat the first number, start from the bigger one); every adult paragraph has a job (curriculum link and research, how to set up, named mistakes, what the lab does). Content gate found no filler phrases and under 12% overlap with any other lesson.

mobile.evidence: Checked 360 px screenshots in light and dark (shot.cjs plus done-state captures): on phones the number track wraps to two rows of five 60 px squares so each is a big tap target, cars are up to 80 px, the 1 to 10 keypad uses two rows of five, fingers are about 40 px wide with a tall hit area, and every scene also has full-width buttons under the canvas. Headings shrink to fit 360 px without clipping.

accessibility.evidence: Every action has a button: Say the jar number, Count a car, Jump to N, Stay on N, Start from N, keypad 1 to 10, Finger up/down, Check and Next. Each action updates the canvas aria-label and c.say live region with the spoken count. The walk.cjs gate ran axe (WCAG 2.1 AA) on desktop and iPhone 13 in both themes with no violations; on-canvas text is dark ink on white chips or the theme text colour on the theme panel.
